os_version: Windows 11 Pro 26100, live in-use desktop (user's real windows present)
app: Whole desktop — 10 concurrent visible windows, 6 process families (elevated WinUI, Chromium x2 modes, Electron, WinUI Notepad, Terminal, Win32 dialog, shell)

stack_detection.method: per-window, from the Win32 map: process image name + elevation token query + open-port probe, BEFORE any content read
stack_detection.signature: chrome.exe+port9235 -> cdp | chrome.exe/Discord.exe/Spotify.exe no port -> uia-latch | Notepad/Terminal/rundll32 -> uia | TokenElevation=True -> pixels-crop

channel_setup: router_win.py: EnumWindows + DwmGetWindowAttribute(CLOAKED) + GetWindowRect + TokenElevation = the compositor map (z-order, geometry, focus, elevation); then best-channel binding per window; content pulled through the bound channel for our probe windows only (privacy rule: the user's windows are mapped and classified, never content-walked).

t1_read_text.detail: Content through the bound channel: timedate dialog via UIA (280 tok, live clock value '14:35:51' in the merged view), our Chrome window via CDP (binding verified on :9235/json; full extraction proven in windows-chrome-cdp). User windows deliberately not read.

t2_enumerate.detail: 10/10 visible windows mapped with z-order, geometry, pid, process, elevation, focus in 1.0 ms / 201 tokens — INCLUDING the elevated Task Manager that is entirely absent from UIA's root enumeration, and including the parked 'LibreOffice ... demande votre autorisation' UAC placeholder (pid unreadable = SYSTEM consent flow, itself a signal). The Win32 map is the layer that keeps the elevated blind spot explicit.

t4_living_screen.detail: Covered by windows-timedate-uia (the same clock, ticking, 80 B/s).

t5_blind_action.detail: The router supplies what the Calculator incident showed is mandatory: before any blind click, (a) the map says which window owns the target rect and whether it is foreground, (b) ControlFromPoint->GetTopLevelControl confirms the owner, (c) elevated targets are pre-declared unclickable (UIPI). These guards blocked a wrong-window click live earlier in the campaign.

t6_pictorial.detail: Windows without a structured channel are routed to pixels EXPLICITLY: the elevated window -> screen-region crop (PrintWindow is also UIPI-blocked); FL-class custom apps -> region-map + crop. Nothing fabricated.

measurements.notes: The merged-view economics on a REAL cluttered desktop: 201-token window map (1 ms) + per-window views on demand (280 tok for the focused dialog) vs 2765 tokens per full-desktop screenshot. Coverage of the 10 windows: 1 cdp, 5 uia, 3 uia-latch, 1 pixels-crop(elevated) — every binding decided from signatures BEFORE reading, 0 silent. Windows' router differs from Linux/macOS in one structural way measured here: the WM map and the semantic channel are SEPARATE trust domains (Win32 sees elevated windows, UIA does not), so the map is not a convenience but the safety mechanism that turns the elevation blind spot from silent to explicit.

runtime_verification.method: full-desktop screenshot captured alongside the map; window rects/z/titles compared
runtime_verification.agreement: map matches the screen incl. the maximized elevated Task Manager in front

permissions_required: none beyond a normal user session; elevated windows readable only as pixels
